chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji‘abi reported to me from Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Salim al-Azdi, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Imran al-Bajali who said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:
Whoever does not have from Allah for himself an admonisher from within his own soul, then the admonitions of the people will never avail him anything.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the importance of self-admonition and the inner conscience?
ai.summary: Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that true moral improvement must begin from within. In this hadith transmitted through a chain of five narrators going back to Muhammad ibn Imran al-Bajali, the Imam explains that whoever does not cultivate an inner voice of self-admonition from Allah cannot benefit from external advice. The teaching addresses the fundamental principle that spiritual growth requires personal accountability — external guidance is ineffective if one’s conscience is not receptive. This was a practical reminder for the early Shi‘a community, emphasizing that sincere self-examination is the prerequisite to benefiting from the counsel of scholars and fellow believers.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 10. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi has reported to me from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Salim al-Azadi, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Imran al-Bijilli who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (as) say:
"Whoever has not been blessed by Allah with an admonishing innerself, he can derive no benefit from the admonitions of the people."
